cryptographic_justification: PQC key encapsulation adds measurable latency. ML-KEM-768 key generation and encapsulation takes longer than X25519 elliptic curve operations. Anomalous duration indicates algorithm mismatch or downgrade.
ML-KEM-768 public key is 1184 bytes vs X25519 32 bytes. PQC handshakes transfer significantly more data. Deviation from expected size indicates misconfiguration or stripping attack.
Failed connections on PQC port indicate active attacks. Downgrade attempts and misconfigured clients produce connection failures not seen in normal PQC traffic.
ML-DSA-65 certificates are 7456 bytes vs RSA-4096 1830 bytes. Server record length directly reflects certificate algorithm. Classical-sized records on PQC port indicate downgrade.
ClientHello with PQC key share is 1400+ bytes. Classical ClientHello is under 400 bytes. Small client records on PQC port indicate missing ML-KEM key share — downgrade indicator.
Time characteristics of PQC handshake follow predictable pattern. Deviations indicate timing attacks or side-channel probing.
ML-KEM-768 key share in ClientHello adds 1088 bytes. Absence of this size increase on PQC port is direct evidence of key share stripping.
Algorithm suite indicator. Absence of ML-KEM-768 on hybrid port directly identifies downgrade or misconfiguration.
Higher security PQC mode. Presence on wrong port indicates misconfiguration.
Classical algorithm indicator. Presence alone on hybrid port indicates successful downgrade attack.
